status_summary: Most of the four recommended steps now have an operative counterpart, but the central request to confine Bostock has not been carried out by the EEOC. Executive Order 14168 (signed 2025-01-20) defines sex as binary, directs enforcement on that basis, and orders agencies to rescind inconsistent guidance, naming EEOC's 2024 harassment guidance; DOJ withdrew two Civil Rights Division memos applying Bostock on 2025-02-12 and stated that Bostock does not require access to single-sex spaces based on gender identity. A Texas federal court vacated the sexual orientation and gender identity parts of EEOC's 2024 harassment guidance on 2025-05-15, DOL rescinded its 2022 WIOA section 188 interpretation on 2026-01-08, and the EEOC voted 2-1 on 2026-01-22 to rescind the entire 2024 harassment guidance. OFCCP published a final rule on 2026-08-21 removing the EO 11246 regulations, including part 60-20 on sex discrimination, effective 2026-10-26; EEOC's sexual orientation and gender identity web page, as fetched on 2026-10-07, still described Bostock-based positions on bathrooms, pronouns and dress, and Bostock remains binding.

timeline.event: President signs EO 14168 (published 2025-01-30). Section 2 defines sex in binary terms, section 3(f) directs the Attorney General to issue guidance on applying Bostock to sex-based distinctions, section 5 directs the Attorney General, Labor Secretary and EEOC to prioritize related enforcement, and section 7(c) directs agencies to rescind inconsistent guidance, naming EEOC's 2024 harassment guidance (7(c)(iv)) and the 2021 DOJ memo applying Bostock to Title IX (7(c)(iii)).

DOJ's Office of the Associate Attorney General issues a memo to the Civil Rights Division citing EO 14168 section 3(f). It states DOJ's position that Bostock, a Title VII employment decision, does not require gender-identity-based access to single-sex spaces or athletics, and withdraws the March 2021 memo applying Bostock to Title IX and the March 2022 memo applying it to other statutes; more detailed guidance was to follow.

In Texas v. EEOC (N.D. Tex., Judge Kacsmaryk), the court vacates the sexual orientation and gender identity portions of EEOC's 2024 harassment guidance, including its bathroom, pronoun and dress examples, per a law firm summary of the ruling; the summary does not say whether EEOC appealed.
timeline.source: Hall Render (law firm summary of court ruling)

timeline.event: DOL publishes a notice rescinding its 2022 interpretation of section 188 of the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act, which had read 'sex' to include transgender status and gender identity; effective immediately.

EEOC Commission votes 2-1 to rescind its 2024 Enforcement Guidance on Harassment in the Workplace in full. EEOC's press release is dated 2026-01-23; Chair Andrea Lucas said the rescission does not permit unlawful harassment and that federal harassment laws and related Supreme Court precedent remain in effect.

OFCCP publishes a final rule (91 FR 54444) removing the EO 11246 regulations at 41 CFR parts 60-1, 60-2, 60-3, 60-4, 60-20, 60-40, 60-50 and 60-999, effective 2026-10-26. Part 60-20 contained the sex discrimination guidelines.

title: Confine Bostock, withdraw gender-identity guidance, and refocus on binary sex

The EEOC release does not name the commissioners who voted; the 2-1 count and the full rescission come from the release and law firm reports. The EEOC SOGI page could be a cached or stale copy even though it was fetched live; no EEOC statement about it was located. The DOJ memo said more detailed guidance would follow; no follow-up guidance was searched for beyond one web search. DOL's 2025-07-02 registered apprenticeship nondiscrimination proposal (which drops a gender identity reference) was not counted here because it is still a proposed rule; see c18-08.
